nodes.label: World ID / Selfie Check integration feedback
nodes.rationale: The protocol behaved exactly as documented; the cost was in undocumented behaviour and in one check that silently moved from World's side to the integrator's. Raw captures are kept in fixtures/worldid/ so every claim is reproducible rather than remembered. Being told plainly that Selfie Check is medium assurance is what let the control be placed where it holds.

nodes.label: v4 signal verification moved to the integrator, silently
nodes.rationale: v3 took the signal explicitly; the v4 endpoint takes only the IDKit payload, so success means 'valid for whatever signal_hash is inside it'. A genuine correctly-signed proof bound to any other context — or to the empty signal an unbound request produces — would have been recorded as authorising a specific payment with nothing looking wrong. Fix: compare responses[].signal_hash against hashSignal(expected) in the backend.

nodes.label: UNIQUE (nullifier, action) is wrong for repeat actions
nodes.rationale: The nullifier is stable per person, so the documented constraint means each human can perform the action exactly once ever — and the failure looks like the control working correctly, so a team shipping the documented schema would find out in production. Scope uniqueness to the signal instead.

nodes.label: Verifier returns success:true on a replayed nullifier
nodes.rationale: HTTP 200 with reuse noted only inside a prose message string, so an integrator gating on success — the obvious thing to gate on — has no replay protection at all and no error to tell them.

nodes.label: created_at is first-seen, not verified-at
nodes.rationale: Two runs hours apart returned an identical created_at, because it timestamps when the nullifier was first ever observed; persisting it as the verification time would have put a wrong timestamp in an audit record.

nodes.label: Field elements are unpadded hex
nodes.rationale: An observed merkle_root came back 63 hex characters in one run and 64 in the next, and nullifiers will be short roughly one time in sixteen, so string storage makes the same person look like two intermittently — breaking continuity for legitimate users and letting a replay through a UNIQUE index.

nodes.label: No way to read whether Selfie Check is enabled for an app
nodes.rationale: No Portal or MCP field reports which credentials an app may request, so the gate that decides whether the integration works at all is invisible to the API describing the app; it was resolved only by building the whole integration and running it — an expensive way to discover a boolean.

nodes.label: Legacy presets can return a different credential than requested
nodes.rationale: Legacy presets return the maximum credential a user has, so selfieCheckLegacy can return an Orb credential and any policy keyed on identifier === 'selfie' rejects your strongest users.
